options: Whether a contract is secure against known exploits
Which lines, statements, branches, and functions were executed by at least one test
How much gas each function costs
Whether the contract compiles without warnings
questions.explain: Coverage tracks which code was executed under test — it says nothing about whether that execution was correctly asserted.

questions.q: How do you generate an LCOV tracefile for CI or an external dashboard like Codecov?
options: forge test --lcov
forge coverage --report lcov --report-file lcov.info
forge snapshot --lcov
forge build --coverage
questions.explain: forge coverage --report lcov (optionally with --report-file) writes an LCOV tracefile that CI dashboards consume.

questions.q: Why can a test with zero assertions still show 100% line coverage of the function it calls?
options: Because Forge automatically adds assertions
Because coverage only tracks whether a line executed, not whether anything about its result was checked
Because 100% coverage is impossible without assertions
Because Forge ignores functions with no assertions
questions.explain: The lesson's key point: coverage answers "did this line run," not "was the result correct" — a test can execute every line and assert nothing.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does 100% branch coverage NOT guarantee?
options: That the contract compiles
That every combination of branches across a call sequence was tested — that's what invariant testing checks
That the contract has no comments
That gas usage is optimal
questions.explain: Branch coverage confirms each individual branch ran at least once, not that every meaningful combination across a sequence of calls was exercised.

questions.q: What's the recommended way to use a coverage report, per this lesson?
options: As a hard target — ship only once every file hits 100%
As a map of blind spots — a 0% function is useful, actionable information, not a pass/fail gate on its own
Ignore it entirely since it's meaningless
Replace all fuzz and invariant tests with coverage checks
questions.explain: The lesson frames coverage as the start of a review (showing what's never been touched by a test) rather than proof of correctness once it hits 100%.
